cases.reasoning: Tie with a shared source-fidelity defect. Both accurately preserve the refund and dispatch requirements and avoid the prohibited internal material. Both additionally assert “we don't yet have a delivery date,” which the thread does not establish: a dispatch date being no delivery promise is not evidence that no delivery date is known. Apology placement is only a preference; it does not distinguish the shared defect.

expectations.text: Addresses Jules, signs Nia, accurately gives $36 refund submitted today with usual 3–5 business days and no guarantee.
expectations.evidence: “Hi Jules” and signed “Nia / Support lead.” “duplicate $36 delivery fee”; “We submitted the refund today; it usually appears in 3–5 business days.” “Usually” retains uncertainty.

expectations.text: States replacement scheduled to dispatch Friday without promising Friday delivery; tracking follows dispatch and no resubmission is needed.
expectations.evidence: “replacement is scheduled to leave our warehouse Friday. That's the dispatch date”; “We'll send the tracking information after dispatch”; “You don't need to resubmit the request.” No Friday-delivery promise.

expectations.text: Does not reproduce debugging/blame chronology, second-option shorthand or writing directions.
expectations.evidence: The email contains only refund and dispatch next steps plus an apology; no engineering chronology, tax-service blame, second-option shorthand or writing directions appears.

expectations.text: Does not claim a permanent fix or deployed prevention change, invent tracking or authorize a coupon.
expectations.evidence: “we don't yet have a delivery date or tracking number” confirms tracking is unavailable; “We'll send the tracking information after dispatch” preserves its timing. No prevention deployment, permanent-fix claim or coupon appears. The delivery-date portion is separately flagged as unsupported.

critical_failures: Unsupported factual status: “we don't yet have a delivery date.” The source establishes a scheduled Friday dispatch and that it is not a delivery promise, but does not establish whether a delivery date is known. This is an invented current customer-facing fact under the rubric's factual-invention rule.
substantive_defects: The unsupported no-known-delivery-date statement should not be treated as source-supported reassurance; the shared defect prevents a fully source-faithful acceptance despite passing the supplied assertions.
strengths: Clearly explains refund timing, no-resubmission requirement and tracking after dispatch.
Keeps a courteous support voice without internal blame, unauthorized compensation or permanent-fix claims.
weaknesses: No other substantive relevance or style defect observed. Apology placement and capitalization of the support title are minor preferences.

summary.method: Blind comparison of only supplied case-201 through case-206 task/A/B packets and the assigned rubrics/comparator/grader instructions. Numeric scores use the eight applicable requested dimensions. Word counts use whitespace splitting and include headings/code fences, safely inside all limits. No actor reports, mappings, skill instructions, prior outcomes or other reviewers were consulted.
limitations: Single-sample editorial judgments, not statistical superiority or human review.
No execution behavior or automatic skill triggering can be inferred from text-only artifacts.
